sections.h2: Rio Rancho and the two-county question
sections.html:
Rio Rancho sits in the Albuquerque Basin, mostly in Sandoval County with a small northern slice in Bernalillo County. It is Sandoval County's largest city, covers about 103.7 square miles at roughly 5,509 feet, and had 114,419 residents at the 2025 estimate, up from 104,046 in 2020.

The split matters when you sell. Most homes are billed by Sandoval County, but a property in the Bernalillo County portion deals with a different assessor and treasurer. Look at your tax bill to see which county it comes from before you call any office.

sections.h2: A planned community with a mix of ages
sections.html:
Rio Rancho began as a land-sales development. In 1961 AMREP bought about 55,000 acres and platted Rio Rancho Estates, and the first families arrived in the early 1960s. The city incorporated in 1981, the year an Intel plant opened and added jobs. Population grew ten-fold between 1970 and 1980 and has kept climbing.

That growth leaves older houses on streets where neighbors have much newer ones, so a buyer will ask about the age of the roof and major systems. After the 2008 housing collapse, foreclosure activity rose here, and the city later adopted an abandoned residential property registration ordinance, covered below.

Intel is the largest employer, followed by the public school district and a hospital. Intel's local headcount has fallen, so home demand can follow that company's news. Retail, services and government fill out the rest.

Rio Rancho is arid, with about 8.90 inches of precipitation a year, because it sits in the rain shadow of the Sandia Mountains and the Continental Divide. The higher western part gets slightly more rain and snow than the denser east side.

Low rainfall does not remove the need for an inspection. A buyer's inspector will still check the roof, drainage around the foundation and exterior finish. An investor or cash buyer prices those items into the offer, so you can skip repairs.

sections.h2: Permits, short-term rentals and abandoned homes
sections.html:
Permits. The Building Division issues permits and inspects construction. Call 505-891-5005 before a home project to ask whether a permit is needed. The city lists the 2021 International Residential Code among its governing codes. Unpermitted work by a past owner can surface during a sale, so gather any permit records you have.

Short-term rentals. Since July 1, 2025, a permit is required to operate, rent, offer to rent or advertise a short-term rental, defined as a stay under 30 days in a single-family residence. A 5% Lodgers' Tax applies, and Development Services can fine up to $500 per day. If your house was used this way, the new owner needs their own permit, so say so early.

Abandoned property. The Governing Body approved an Abandoned Residential Property Registration ordinance in December 2011. If a house is vacant after an owner dies or moves out, read the ordinance on the Code Enforcement pages.

The Sandoval County Assessor values the property and the Treasurer collects. A Notice of Value goes out by April 1 each year and you have 30 days from mailing to protest. The notice is not a bill.

DateWhat happens
January 1Property is assessed to the owner of record, and taxes are a lien from this date
April 1Notice of Value is due to be mailed
30 days after mailingLast day to file a valuation protest or claim an exemption
November 1Tax bills mailed
November 10 and December 10First half due, then delinquent after December 10
April 10 and May 10Second half due, then delinquent after May 10

Taxable value is one-third of assessed value, minus exemptions. New Mexico has no homestead exemption. It has a Head of Family exemption, described as $2,000 off taxable value for a primary residence. If a property changes hands after January 1, the exemption comes off the next January 1 and the new owner must apply.

A deed must be recorded with the county clerk before the assessor updates the owner. If you close with a title company, it records the deed for you. Taxes unpaid for two years can lead to a state auction, so a seller with old balances should settle them or sell before then. Ask the title company how tax and any liens will be handled at closing, and keep copies of every document.

Rio Rancho Public Schools serves most of the city. Parts fall in the Jemez Valley Public Schools district, and much of the Bernalillo County portion is zoned to Albuquerque Public Schools. Buyers often start with the district boundary, so confirm which one your address belongs to before describing it.

ABQ RIDE route 251 connects Rio Rancho to the Rail Runner station at Journal Center, and Rio Metro runs commuter buses toward the US 550 Rail Runner station. Albuquerque borders the city to the south, so many residents commute by road.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a Rio Rancho house
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who purchases as-is.

  • List with an agent: the widest exposure, plus showings, inspections and repair requests.
  • Sell it yourself: saves a commission but leaves marketing, paperwork and negotiation to you.
  • Cash offer: the buyer takes the house as it stands, so repairs and cleaning are not your job. Ask for the offer in writing and compare it with what you would net on the other two routes.

Cash can suit an inherited house, back payments, a rental with tenants, or a house that needs work.

sections.h2: Steps before you accept an offer
sections.html: Confirm which county bills your property, pull the latest tax statement, and gather permit records and any short-term rental permit paperwork. Decide whether you want to wait for a financed buyer or prefer speed. Then choose a title company and ask in advance how tax, liens and closing costs will be divided.

faqs.q: How many people live in Rio Rancho?
faqs.a: The 2025 estimate is 114,419 residents, and the 2020 census counted 104,046. It is the largest city in Sandoval County.

faqs.q: Which county is Rio Rancho in?
faqs.a: Most of it is in Sandoval County, with a small northern portion in Bernalillo County. Your tax bill shows which county's assessor and treasurer handle your property.

faqs.q: When are Sandoval County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are mailed by November 1. The first half is due November 10 and delinquent after December 10, and the second half is due April 10 and delinquent after May 10.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to run a short-term rental in Rio Rancho?
faqs.a: Yes. Since July 1, 2025, a permit is required to operate, rent or advertise one, and a 5% Lodgers' Tax applies. Fines can reach $500 per day.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Rio Rancho house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Sell it as-is to a cash buyer, or list it and negotiate repairs after inspection. Compare the net amount from each route.
